title: R' Yehudah ben Pazi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Zohar Chadash, Bereishit, in the section “And God said: Let there be a firmament.” R' Yosi ben Chalafta and R' Yehudah ben Pazi were eating at the wedding feast of R' Elazar son of R' Shimon, and R' Chiyya was sitting there as a child. They said, “Let us ask this child,” etc. If this is a received tradition, we will accept it; for R' Chiyya is known to have been a Babylonian who went up to the Land of Israel only when he was already a leading sage of his generation, as explained in his entry.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The conditional acceptance and chronological objection are Hyman’s comment, not part of the Zohar account. The names in ר״י בן חלפתא, ר״י בן פזי and ר״א בר״ש follow their customary/contextual readings, while their abbreviated titles remain R'; these do not establish external identities. The heading’s tanna label is retained despite the older OCR’s different reading. No precise Zohar folio is supplied, no missing dialogue is reconstructed, and neither the cited account nor Hyman’s chronology was independently checked.

The personal titles abbreviated in Hyman remain R' here: no exact title-bearing Zohar Chadash passage was checked. The names and Hyman’s conditional acceptance are retained without a new identification or chronological ruling.
